subject: Re: VectorHive — Q3 capacity top-up & co-term pricing request
messages:
From: Tom Park <tom.park@vectorhive.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 capacity top-up and co-term with Redwood

Hi Markus,

Hope you’re well — quick heads up from our side. We’ve got a campaign kicking off mid-August with expected burst traffic that will push our token consumption ~50% above our current committed capacity for at least Q3. Can Redwood accommodate a mid-quarter top-up that gets applied to our existing commitment and co-terms everything to our current renewal date (01/31/2027)?

Questions from procurement:
- How would pro-rata pricing work for a top-up today vs. adding a temporary burst bucket?
- Will we keep our current discount tier applied to the incremental capacity or does it reset?
- Do you have a sample SOW/quote we can route to procurement?

I attached a short usage summary. We’d like ballpark options today and a formal quote by early next week if possible.

Thanks,
Tom
VP Product
VectorHive

Attachment: VectorHive_usage_summary.csv

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Q3 capacity top-up and co-term with Redwood

Team — forwarding VectorHive’s ask. Key asks: +50% capacity for Q3, co-term to 2027-01-31, procurement needs a quote/SOW.

Quick constraints/context:
- Current committed monthly throughput: 4M tokens/month (commit).
- They want an uplift of 2M tokens/month for Aug–Oct (approx).
- They’re currently in Tier 2 discount (7%) on committed spend.

Can we:
1) Outline two paths (temporary burst vs permanent uplift with pro-rata co-term) with math.
2) Confirm whether their current tier extends to incremental capacity if we co-term.
3) Produce a quote stub they can send to procurement (pdf).

I’m happy to take the customer call if you want me there — need this turned around fast.

— Markus

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Q3 capacity top-up and co-term with Redwood

Markus — draft options below. I ran the numbers against their usage summary and current contract. Attaching a formal quote (Redwood_TopUp_Quote_v1.pdf).

Option A — Temporary Burst (fastest, lowest commitment)
- Add burst bucket: +2M tokens/month for Aug–Oct as a metered add-on.
- Rate: $0.012/token for burst (no change to committed pricing).
- No change to co-term; bucket expires 10/31/2026.
- Procurement: simple PO for metered add-on; minimal contract work.

Option B — Permanent Top-up + Co-term (preferred for unit economics)
- Convert +2M tokens/month into committed capacity, co-term all commitments to 2027-01-31.
- Pro-rata charge for the remainder of the current contract period (prorated to days).
- Apply existing Tier 2 discount to the newly committed capacity if they co-term now (company policy: we preserve tiering on expansion when co-termed).
- Effective blended discount: 7% on existing + 7% on new capacity.
- If they commit to a 12-month price lock for the uplift we can offer +2% discount (total 9% on the uplift) — requires PO within 7 days.

Numbers (approx):
- List price / token: $0.015
- Current monthly committed tokens: 4,000,000 => after 7% discount = effective $0.01395/token
- Proposed added commit: 2,000,000 tokens => after 7% = $0.01395/token, with early-PO incentive reduces to $0.01371/token

Procurement artifacts: attached quote + standard SOW. If VectorHive needs a line-item for SSO/KMS, we can add.

Notes: Option B gives them better unit cost and simplifies billing; Option A is quick but more expensive.

— Laura
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_TopUp_Quote_v1.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Tom — thanks for the note and the usage file.

Forwarding two quick paths from Laura (attached): temporary burst (fastest) or convert to committed uplift + co-term (better price). I’ve included a one-page quote for procurement to review.

Summary for procurement: 
- Option A (burst): quick PO, no contract changes, higher per-token rate.
- Option B (top-up + co-term): prorated charge today, keep tiering, opportunity for additional 2% off uplift if PO signed within 7 days for price lock.

Would you be available for a 30-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the quote and get alignment on timelines? If they want us to take the co-term route we’ll need a short redline (we typically attach an amendment).

Best,
Markus
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_TopUp_Quote_v1.pdf

3) Everyone: 30-min alignment call tomorrow 10am PT to confirm SOW line items (SSO/KMS, logging retention).
